definitionEn: stated clearly and in detail, leaving no doubt about what is meant
senseNote: Здесь — «прямо и чётко выраженный»; значение «откровенный (о сценах секса или насилия)» не рассматривается.
situation: Describing instructions, rules or statements that say something directly and precisely, so nobody can misunderstand them.

examples.text: Our manager gave [[explicit]] instructions not to share the figures, so nobody can say they didn't know.
The author is quite [[explicit]] about her political views, so readers know exactly where she stands.
You need the owner's [[explicit]] permission before you publish any of these photos.

texts: Be [[explicit]] about what you expect from the team this month.
Her message was short but [[explicit]]: no more late submissions.
The rules on overtime should be made [[explicit]] in every contract.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Явное преимущество» — a clear или an obvious advantage. Explicit — о том, что прямо сказано или записано: указания, правила, разрешение.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое сочетание — make no explicit mention of: «прямо не упоминать». Notice, saying и telling с make в этом значении не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The ban on phones is [[explicit]]: it's printed in bold on the first page of the rules.
nuance.explanationRu: Explicit — прямо высказанный или записанный. Implicit — подразумеваемый, невысказанный. Запрет, напечатанный жирным шрифтом, никак не «подразумевается».

reverse.text: Nobody said it aloud, but there was an [[implicit]] agreement not to discuss salaries.
reverse.explanationRu: Договорённость, о которой никто не говорил вслух, — implicit. Explicit она была бы, если бы её прямо сформулировали.

fixIt.text: Staff need the client's [[obvious]] permission before recording any calls.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Явное разрешение» — explicit permission, то есть данное прямо. Obvious значит «очевидный» и с permission не сочетается.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Did the client say we could use their logo on our website?"
options: Yes, and their logo is really explicit, with bright colours and huge letters.
Yes, they gave us explicit permission in Monday's email, so we're fine.
Affirmative. Explicit authorisation was hereby granted by the aforementioned client.
reply.explanationRu: Explicit permission — прямое, чётко выраженное разрешение. Логотип не бывает explicit в значении «яркий». Третий вариант звучит как канцелярский документ, а не ответ коллеге.

rewrite.original: She told us very clearly what she expected from us.
rewrite.frame: She was very ____ about what she expected from us.
rewrite.explanationRu: Be explicit about something — «говорить о чём-то прямо и чётко».

definitionEn: in a clear, direct way that leaves no doubt about the meaning
situation: Saying or writing something directly and precisely, so that nobody can misunderstand it or pretend they did not know.

examples.text: The job advert [[explicitly]] asks for candidates with at least five years of experience.
I [[explicitly]] asked you not to tell anyone, and now the whole office knows!
The novel never [[explicitly]] names the city, but readers soon guess it is Paris.

texts: The email [[explicitly]] says that the offer ends on Friday.
She never [[explicitly]] criticised her boss in the interview.
The law [[explicitly]] protects workers who report fraud.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Явно лучше» — clearly или obviously better. Explicitly — «прямо, открытым текстом»: так говорят о словах, правилах и документах.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Правила и документы прямо что-то запрещают — explicitly forbid. Loudly, sincerely и visibly описывают людей: как они говорят, чувствуют или выглядят.

nuance.text: Could you say it more [[explicitly]]? I still don't understand what you want.
nuance.explanationRu: Explicitly — сказать прямо и чётко, без намёков. Obviously — «очевидно», это оценка ситуации, а не способ говорить; «say it more obviously» звучит странно.

reverse.text: It's [[obviously]] too late to change the plan now.
reverse.explanationRu: Когда вывод очевиден сам по себе, нужен obviously. Explicitly описывает, как что-то сказано или записано.

fixIt.text: Your contract [[openly]] states that you must give a month's notice.
fixIt.explanationRu: Openly — «открыто, не скрывая», так говорят о людях и их чувствах. Если документ прямо что-то оговаривает, он explicitly states.

wordFormation.text: The label [[explicitly]] warns against giving the medicine to young children.

rewrite.original: Nobody told us directly that the project had been cancelled.
rewrite.frame: We were never ____ that the project had been cancelled.
rewrite.explanationRu: Пассив с наречием: we were never explicitly told — «нам прямо не говорили».

definitionEn: the unfair treatment of people, using their work or weakness for profit
senseNote: Здесь — нечестное использование людей ради выгоды; значение «разработка (природных ресурсов)» не рассматривается.
situation: Talking about workers, children or vulnerable people who are used unfairly and badly paid so that someone else gets rich.

examples.text: The documentary exposes the [[exploitation]] of migrant workers on fruit farms, where many earn almost nothing.
Working sixty hours a week for no pay is pure [[exploitation]], not work experience.
Our history lecturer showed how the sugar trade grew rich through the [[exploitation]] of enslaved people.

texts: Fair-trade coffee is meant to reduce the [[exploitation]] of small farmers.
The charity helps teenagers escape [[exploitation]] by criminal gangs.
The union accused the delivery company of the systematic [[exploitation]] of drivers.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Эксплуатационные расходы» — running или operating costs. Exploitation в английском — прежде всего нечестное использование людей.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Эксплуатация людей — exploitation. Operation, usage и maintenance — это «эксплуатация» техники или зданий, к людям они не подходят.

nuance.text: Campaigners want an end to the [[exploitation]] of domestic workers.
nuance.explanationRu: Exploitation — нечестное использование людей ради выгоды. Misuse — неправильное использование вещей, денег, лекарств или власти; о людях так не говорят.

reverse.text: A council official resigned over the [[misuse]] of public funds.
reverse.explanationRu: Нецелевое использование денег — misuse of funds. Exploitation говорят о людях, которых используют ради выгоды.

fixIt.text: The report describes the [[exploration]] of factory workers who earn less than two euros an hour.
fixIt.explanationRu: Exploration — исследование. Нечестное использование чужого труда — exploitation.

wordFormation.text: Human rights groups warn that the new visa rules could lead to the [[exploitation]] of foreign workers.

reply.context: A friend messages: "I got an internship at a top agency! It's unpaid and six days a week, for a whole year."
options: Congratulations! That's a brilliant exploitation of your talents.
We hereby acknowledge that the arrangement may constitute exploitation.
Congratulations, but a year without pay sounds like exploitation to me.
reply.explanationRu: Exploitation — нечестное использование чужого труда, и год без оплаты — именно это. «Exploitation of your talents» в поздравлении не говорят, а второй вариант звучит как официальное письмо.

definitionEn: likely to cause strong feelings, angry arguments or sudden violence
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «взрывоопасный, грозящий конфликтом»; прямое значение «взрывчатый» (B2) не рассматривается.
situation: Describing a topic, situation or piece of news that could easily lead to angry arguments, protests or violence.

examples.text: The leaked emails could be politically [[explosive]] if they reach the press before the election.
Don't bring up pay cuts at the meeting: it's an [[explosive]] subject right now.
The atmosphere at dinner was [[explosive]]: my parents and my brother were shouting at each other within minutes.

texts: Pension reform remains an [[explosive]] issue in many countries.
The family meeting turned [[explosive]] when someone mentioned the will.
Rising rents and falling wages are an [[explosive]] combination.

badCollocation.noteRu: Весёлую, зажигательную вечеринку называют a lively или a wild party. Explosive о ситуации значит «взрывоопасный, грозящий скандалом».

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Взрывоопасная тема» — an explosive issue. Exploding, blasting и bursting описывают сам взрыв или разрыв, а не опасную тему.

nuance.text: By Friday the mood outside the factory was [[explosive]], and police had been called.
nuance.explanationRu: Explosive — накалённый, готовый взорваться гневом. Sensitive — деликатный: о теме, которую обсуждают осторожно, но не о настроении толпы у ворот завода.

reverse.text: Please treat this information as [[sensitive]] and don't forward it to anyone.
reverse.explanationRu: Конфиденциальную, деликатную информацию называют sensitive. Explosive — о том, что может вызвать скандал или вспышку гнева.

fixIt.text: Closing the village school proved politically [[sharp]]: the first public meeting ended in shouting.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Острый» в значении «грозящий конфликтом» — explosive. Sharp так не употребляют: это «острый» о ноже, боли или уме.

wordFormation.text: Water shortages have made the situation in the region highly [[explosive]].

reply.context: Your manager asks: "Should I mention the bonus cuts in tomorrow's team meeting?"
options: I'd wait. It's an explosive subject, and people are already stressed.
Definitely! It's such explosive news that everyone will be delighted.
Yo, just drop it on them, it'll be totally explosive lol.
reply.explanationRu: Explosive — «взрывоопасный, грозящий конфликтом», поэтому с новостью о бонусах лучше подождать. Радостная новость explosive не бывает, а третий вариант слишком фамильярен для разговора с начальником.

definitionEn: the outside part or surface of something, especially a building or vehicle
senseNote: Здесь — наружная часть здания или предмета; переносное «внешняя маска» (a calm exterior) не рассматривается.
situation: Talking about the outside walls, paint or surface of a building, car or object, as opposed to the inside.

examples.text: The [[exterior]] of the museum is all cold glass and steel, but inside it feels warm and cosy.
The car's [[exterior]] is in perfect condition, but the seats are torn and the radio is broken.
Planning rules protect the [[exterior]] of historic buildings, but owners can modernise the inside.

texts: The hotel's [[exterior]] is plain, but the rooms are stunning.
Wipe the [[exterior]] of the jar before you put it back in the fridge.
Engineers checked the [[exterior]] of the capsule after its return from space.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Судить по внешности» — judge people by their appearance (или by appearances). Exterior — наружная сторона здания, машины или предмета.

collocationTask.prompt: restore the ___ of the old station
collocationTask.explanationRu: Наружная часть здания — the exterior (или the outside). Outer и external — прилагательные и без существительного не стоят, а outdoors — «на улице, на природе».

nuance.text: We repainted the whole [[exterior]] of the house, including the back wall.
nuance.explanationRu: Facade — лицевая, парадная сторона здания. Exterior — вся наружная часть со всех сторон, поэтому с «including the back wall» подходит только exterior.

fixIt.text: The [[outlook]] of the new library is very modern, but the reading rooms feel old-fashioned.
fixIt.explanationRu: Outlook — взгляд на жизнь или прогноз, а не внешний вид. Наружная сторона здания — exterior.

reply.context: A friend who is house-hunting texts: "How was the flat you viewed today?"
options: The exterior is lovely: two big bedrooms and a modern kitchen.
The exterior of the premises was deemed satisfactory upon inspection.
The building's exterior is a bit grim, but the flat itself is bright and spacious.
reply.explanationRu: Exterior — наружная часть здания, спальни и кухня к ней не относятся. Второй вариант звучит как отчёт инспектора, а не ответ другу.

definitionEn: to get information, money or a promise from someone who is unwilling to give it
senseNote: Здесь — «вытягивать сведения, признание, обещание»; прямое значение «извлекать, удалять» (B2) не рассматривается.
situation: Getting a secret, a promise, money or a confession from someone who really does not want to give it.

examples.text: The reporter tried every trick she knew to [[extract]] details of the deal from the nervous official.
It took me all evening to [[extract]] the name of her new boyfriend from my sister.
After weeks of talks, the union managed to [[extract]] a promise of higher wages from management.

texts: It's almost impossible to [[extract]] a straight answer from him.
Scammers invent fake emergencies to [[extract]] money from elderly people.
Journalists tried to [[extract]] a comment from the company's lawyers.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Извлечь вывод» — draw a conclusion, «извлечь урок» — learn a lesson. Extract в этом значении — вытянуть из человека сведения, деньги или обещание.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Добиться признания — extract a confession from someone. Make или give a confession — «признаться самому», с from так не говорят; do с confession не сочетается.

nuance.text: The head teacher finally [[extracted]] an apology from the boy who had broken the window.
nuance.explanationRu: Extract — добиться чего-то с трудом и упорством. Extort — вымогать угрозами или силой, это преступление; к извинениям школьника оно не подходит.

fixIt.text: It took the police hours to [[take out]] the truth from the witness.
fixIt.explanationRu: Take out — вынуть что-то физически. Добиться правды или признания от человека — extract (the truth) from someone.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Did you find out from Mark when the new office will open?"
options: Yes, I extracted him a quick email this morning.
I tried, but extracting any real information from him is like pulling teeth.
The requisite data has been extracted from the aforementioned individual.
reply.explanationRu: Extract information from someone — «вытягивать сведения из того, кто не хочет говорить». «Extracted him an email» — бессмыслица, а третий вариант звучит как полицейский протокол.

rewrite.original: She finally got him to promise that he would call every day.
rewrite.frame: She finally ____ from him to call every day.
rewrite.explanationRu: Extract a promise from someone — «добиться от кого-то обещания».

definitionEn: a person with very radical political or religious views who may support violence
situation: Talking about people whose radical beliefs make them ready to use or support violence to change society.

examples.text: The forum was closed after [[extremists]] began using it to spread hatred and recruit teenagers.
Her thesis explores why some well-educated students become [[extremists]] and reject democracy altogether.
Don't call everyone who disagrees with you an [[extremist]]; that's just lazy thinking.

texts: The security services are watching a small group of [[extremists]] in the city.
Social media companies are under pressure to ban [[extremists]] from their platforms.
Most voters reject [[extremists]] on both sides of the debate.

badCollocation.noteRu: Любитель экстрима — a thrill-seeker или an adrenaline junkie. Extremist — человек с радикальными политическими или религиозными взглядами.

collocationTask.prompt: the police arrested a group of ___
collocationTask.explanationRu: Людей с радикальными взглядами называют extremists. Extremism — сама идеология, extremes — крайности, extremities — конечности (руки и ноги).

nuance.text: The judge said he was not a peaceful protester but a violent [[extremist]] who wanted to hurt people.
nuance.explanationRu: Activist — активист, который борется за идею мирно. Extremist — сторонник крайних взглядов, готовый к насилию; «violent activist» здесь звучит противоречиво.

reverse.text: She's an environmental [[activist]] who organises beach clean-ups every month.
reverse.explanationRu: Человек, который мирно борется за экологию, — activist. Extremist — это обвинение в радикализме и готовности к насилию.

fixIt.text: The government is worried about [[extremism]] who recruit teenagers online.
fixIt.explanationRu: Extremism — идеология, а who требует людей: extremists who recruit — «экстремисты, которые вербуют».

wordFormation.text: The conference discussed ways to fight online [[extremism]] among young people.

definitionEn: relating to the front of a person's head, where the eyes, nose and mouth are
situation: Describing expressions, hair, muscles or features on someone's head, or technology that identifies people from their looks.

examples.text: Babies learn to read [[facial]] expressions long before they understand words.
The airport now uses [[facial]] recognition to check passengers' identities at the gate.
Company rules on [[facial]] hair are strict: kitchen staff must be clean-shaven or wear a beard net.

texts: Actors train their [[facial]] muscles as carefully as their voices.
The accident left him with a small [[facial]] scar above the lip.
The twins have identical [[facial]] features but very different personalities.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Лицевая сторона» документа или ткани — the front или the right side. Facial относится только к лицу человека: facial expression, facial hair.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Выражение лица — facial expression. «Мимика» — не mimic (это «подражать»), а look и sight с facial не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Scientists studied the [[facial]] expressions of people watching horror films.
nuance.explanationRu: С expression, features, hair и muscles нужно прилагательное facial. Face как определение живёт в бытовых словах: face cream, face mask.

reverse.text: Visitors must wear a [[face]] mask in all areas of the hospital.
reverse.explanationRu: Медицинская маска — a face mask. Facial mask — косметическая маска для кожи, в больнице так не говорят.

fixIt.text: The actor grew so much [[face]] hair for the role that fans didn't recognise him.
fixIt.explanationRu: Волосы на лице — facial hair. Face как определение бывает в бытовых сочетаниях (face cream), но не с hair.

wordFormation.text: The surgeon specialises in repairing [[facial]] injuries after car accidents.

reply.context: At an interview with a security company, you're asked: "What do you know about our new camera system?"
options: I read that it scans the facial side of ID cards.
Dunno, something about faces? Facial stuff, I guess.
I read that it uses facial recognition to let staff into the building.
reply.explanationRu: Facial recognition — распознавание лиц, это и есть работа такой системы. «Facial side» — калька с «лицевая сторона», а второй ответ слишком небрежен для собеседования.

rewrite.original: He never shows what he is feeling on his face.
rewrite.frame: His ____ never show what he is feeling.

definitionEn: to make a process or action easier or more likely to happen
senseNote: Основное значение — «облегчать, содействовать»; специальное «вести обсуждение или тренинг» не рассматривается.
situation: Talking formally about how a tool, rule or person makes a process smoother, faster or simpler.

examples.text: The new software should [[facilitate]] communication between our offices, so projects will move faster.
Small groups [[facilitate]] discussion, so every student gets a chance to speak.
Lower interest rates are meant to [[facilitate]] borrowing for small businesses.

texts: Clear signs help to [[facilitate]] the flow of visitors through the museum.
The council promised to [[facilitate]] the building of affordable homes.
A good interpreter can [[facilitate]] trust between the two sides.

badCollocation.noteRu: Facilitate не сочетается с человеком: говорят help students (to) learn или facilitate students' learning.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Сделать доступ проще — facilitate access. Lighten облегчает вес или настроение, soften смягчает, loosen ослабляет — с access они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The new ramps [[facilitate]] access for wheelchair users.
nuance.explanationRu: Facilitate — облегчать процесс или действие. Relieve — облегчать боль, стресс или тяжесть; «relieve access» не говорят.

reverse.text: This cream should [[relieve]] the itching in a few minutes.
reverse.explanationRu: Облегчить боль, зуд или стресс — relieve. Facilitate облегчает процессы, а не неприятные ощущения.

fixIt.text: The new online form should [[alleviate]] the application process for students.
fixIt.explanationRu: Alleviate — облегчать страдания, бедность или острую проблему. Облегчить процесс или действие — facilitate.

wordFormation.text: The workshop was led by an experienced [[facilitator]] who kept the discussion focused.

reply.context: In a meeting, your manager asks: "Why should we move all our files to a shared drive?"
options: It would facilitate collaboration: everyone could work on the same documents.
It would facilitate our boss, so he has less work to do.
Cos it's way easier, innit? Facilitates stuff and that.
reply.explanationRu: Facilitate collaboration — «облегчить совместную работу». Человека facilitate нельзя, а третий вариант слишком фамильярен для рабочей встречи.

rewrite.original: The new bridge will make it much easier to trade between the two towns.
rewrite.frame: The new bridge will ____ between the two towns.

definitionEn: a small group within a larger organisation or party that disagrees with the rest
situation: Talking about a group inside a party, club or organisation that opposes other members and fights for its own aims.

examples.text: Two [[factions]] within the party are fighting over who should become the next leader.
Our book club has two [[factions]] now: the crime fans and the people who only read classics.
In the seminar, we compared how each [[faction]] used newspapers to win public support during the revolution.

texts: The rebel [[factions]] finally agreed to share power.
The club's two [[factions]] refuse to sit at the same table.
Feuding [[factions]] inside the company slowed down every decision.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Значительная часть населения» — a large proportion или section of the population. Faction — организованная группировка внутри партии или организации.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Соперничающие группировки — rival (или opposing) factions. Opposite, contrary и adverse с faction не сочетаются: они описывают направления, мнения и последствия.

nuance.text: A breakaway [[faction]] of the party voted against its own leader.
nuance.explanationRu: Faction — группировка внутри одной партии или организации. Coalition — союз нескольких партий; «коалиция партии», голосующая против своего лидера, невозможна.

reverse.text: After the election, three parties formed a [[coalition]] to govern the country.
reverse.explanationRu: Союз нескольких партий для управления страной — coalition. Faction — лишь часть одной партии.

fixIt.text: The more radical [[fraction]] of the party wants to leave the government.
fixIt.explanationRu: Русское «фракция» — это faction. Fraction — «доля» или «дробь»: a fraction of the price.

reply.context: A friend who works at a start-up says: "Half the team wants to go fully remote, and the other half wants the office back. It's getting tense."
options: It is imperative that the factions be reconciled without further delay.
Sounds like you've got two factions. Could your manager suggest a compromise?
Sounds like a big faction of the budget goes on rent, then.
reply.explanationRu: Faction — группировка внутри коллектива, здесь это две противоположные группы. «Faction of the budget» — путаница с fraction, а первый вариант звучит как официальное заявление.
